description: Master Plan Unified V206 formalizes the hardware integration of the Intel Core i9-12900K (8 efficiency, 8 performance cores) on an ASUS TUF Gaming Z790-Plus WiFi motherboard within the V4 physical shell. The V4 shell is a three-tiered structure: a wooden rolling base salvaged from a speaker project, a modified metal Thermaltake Mozart midrange, and a plastic 2005 WowWee animatronic monkey head top controlled by Arduino boards. The Lenovo Legion Go runs Windows 11 Insider Preview Pro and is strictly dedicated LabTech, completely excluded from core Huey runtime. The V1 proof pipeline has been removed. External heat exchange is paused pending shell completion. Storage includes four Intel Optane M10 16GB drives in RAID 10 for OS and two 10TB HDDs in RAID 1 for data. Power is planned as dual 1000W PSUs (Corsair RM1000x provisional) linked via Add2PSU. Four NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB GPUs are targeted to provide 128GB pooled VRAM (one currently on hand), with a discrete 16GB GPU planned for display. Python 3.13 is core, 3.12 side-carded, 3.14 testing. Only Dylan L.R. Pollock may lock canon.

explicit_decisions: The project is organized around Huey Brain, Huey Body, and Huey Farm.

A Huey node is designed as a physically individual AI unit with integrated local compute, brain, and body functions. Standalone operation is central; collective membership is a long-term goal and not required for the first node to be valid.
Huey V4 physical shell assembly merges V2 and V3 parts with additional lab materials.

V4 physical structure is three-tiered: a wooden base salvaged from a speaker project (with robust caster wheels and internal speakers), a metal midrange utilizing the modified Thermaltake Mozart case (upside down, backwards, highly modified), and a plastic top featuring the 2005 WowWee animatronic monkey head.

The V4 top animatronic head is controlled by Arduino boards; the plan is to merge a pristine unit and a test unit, removing rubber, focusing on basic mouth movement, with a possible detachable head design and avoiding full gutting.
An animatronic hand is attached for programming and testing, not primary function.
V4 physical finish scheme: primer base followed by a latex-based metallic silver color coat with deep purple and black accents; no clear coat.
Final assembly height will be approximately 6 feet or more, constrained by doorway and room fan clearance.
Primary project storage consists of two 10 TB hard drives configured in a RAID 1 array for data redundancy.
OS storage consists of four Intel Optane M10 16GB drives in a RAID 10 array for mirrored striped performance, yielding 32GB usable space.
Huey Brain core workstation hardware is confirmed as an ASUS TUF Gaming Z790-Plus WiFi motherboard paired with an Intel Core i9-12900K processor (8 efficiency cores, 8 performance cores).
Lenovo Legion Go is running Windows 11 Insider Preview Pro and is strictly dedicated LabTech, completely excluded from Huey Brain, Body, and Farm core runtime execution.
The V1 proof pipeline has been completely removed to prevent conflict with the V4 robotic shell assembly.
Four Nvidia Tesla V100 32 GB GPUs are targeted to be pooled to provide 128 GB of VRAM for large-model hosting; currently only one V100 is on hand.
A fifth discrete graphics card (target 16GB VRAM) provides display output and system boot graphics, and may offset smaller tasks such as audio transcription; not yet acquired.
All five PCIe devices (four V100s and one discrete GPU) connect via PCIe extenders; extenders are on hand but untested and may need replacement.
Power delivery relies on dual 1000W PSUs linked via an Add2PSU adapter; model narrowed to Corsair RM1000x but not yet acquired.
Cooling relies on provisional traditional air heat sink; the external Canadian winter heat exchange room is paused until the physical shell is finished.
The target canonical Python namespace is hueyos, explicitly supporting Python 3.13, with Python 3.12 packages side-carded for PyGPT compatibility, and Python 3.14 under testing.
HIMS (Huey Internal Messaging System) serves as Huey's internal mail and communication service between sandboxed internal nodes, mandating end-to-end encryption.
Documentation layers (Master Plan, README, dlrp.ca) must remain synchronized while maintaining distinct authoritative purposes.
Project code is licensed under GPL-3.0, though other components may be subject to varied licenses.
Only Dylan L.R. Pollock may lock project canon.
source_priority: older plans, transcripts, and archives as lineage
source_basis.inheritance_policy: Carry forward previous implementation evidence and lineage unless Unified V206 explicitly changes the direction. Do not present target-state decisions as already implemented.

truth_model.definition: Observed hardware, merged code, working commands, and directly verified behavior.
Architecture Dylan has selected for implementation, even when migration is incomplete.
A working selection that remains replaceable through evidence.
A decision intentionally left open pending additional detail or testing.
A longer-term capability whose implementation depends on resources, maturity, or later validation.
Earlier systems and decisions retained for continuity without overriding current direction.

canon.rule: No agent, tool, contributor, generated document, branch, or pull request may independently lock canon.
acceptance_mechanisms: Dylan intentionally merges a designated canonical update
canon.conflict_rule: Current explicit decisions override older documentation; implementation reality must still be labelled separately from accepted direction.

node_first_architecture.principle: A Huey node is a physically individual AI unit with integrated local compute, brain, and body functions.
node_first_architecture.standalone_operation: Standalone operation is central to the architecture; the first node must be valid without collective membership.
node_first_architecture.collective_membership: The long-term goal facilitates collective membership and shared infrastructure across multiple nodes, but the initial deployment focuses fully on the viability of a single physical system.

three_part_architecture.decision: Organize the system around Huey Brain, Huey Body, and Huey Farm.

current_platform.system: ASUS TUF Gaming Z790-Plus WiFi motherboard with Intel Core i9-12900K processor (8 P-cores, 8 E-cores)
current_platform.housing: Thermaltake Mozart case (midrange of V4 shell, upside down, backwards, highly modified)
current_platform.purpose: Primary workstation, orchestration hub, and execution platform for Huey Brain
current_platform.storage: OS: four Intel Optane M10 16GB drives in RAID 10 (32GB usable); Data: two 10 TB hard drives in RAID 1 array

huey_body.current_boundary: V4 physical shell assembly is a three-tiered structure. The base is wood salvaged from a speaker project featuring robust caster wheels and four internal speakers. The speakers are wired in but not yet connected to the Boss marine-grade amplifier. The midrange is the modified metal Thermaltake Mozart case (upside down, backwards), housing the motherboard. The top is a plastic 2005 WowWee animatronic monkey head controlled by Arduino boards, with an attached animatronic hand for programming. The exterior finish is primer coated with a latex-based metallic silver paint with deep purple and black accents. Final height is approximately 6 feet or more, constrained by doorway and room fan clearance.
huey_body.integration_rule: Brain and Body integration requires explicit interfaces, operator-visible state, safe-stop behavior, and recovery procedures.

huey_farm.role: Scalable compute, model, storage, and support infrastructure.
huey_farm.planning_scale: 128 GB pooled local VRAM targeted across four Nvidia Tesla V100 32 GB GPUs to comfortably host large open-source models; one V100 currently on hand.
huey_farm.power_delivery: Dual 1000W PSUs (Corsair RM1000x provisional) linked via Add2PSU adapter for stable, high-capacity load distribution.
